Book club discussion questions for any book

4 min read · Updated: 23 November 2026

Good questions turn a polite summary round into a real conversation. Below are question sets you can use for almost any book, how to order them, and a quick way to generate questions for a specific title with AI.

TL;DR
  • Open with personal questions, move to the ideas, end with “what will you do differently?”.
  • Six to eight questions are enough for an hour.
  • AI can draft questions for any book in a minute; a human should pick the best ones.

What makes a good book club question?

A good question has no single right answer and connects the book to the reader's own life. “Did you like it?” ends in a yes or no. “Which idea would you actually try at work, and what would stop you?” gets people telling stories, disagreeing politely and remembering the book weeks later.

Questions for any nonfiction book

  1. What was the one idea you underlined or remembered first?
  2. Which claim in the book did you not believe? Why?
  3. Where does the author's advice not fit your life, job or culture?
  4. If you had to explain the book to a 12-year-old in two sentences, what would you say?
  5. Which example or story from the book stayed with you?
  6. What would the opposite of this book's main idea look like? Is it ever true?
  7. Which small thing will you do differently this month because of the book?
  8. Who should not read this book?

Questions for any novel

  1. Which character would you most like to meet, and which would you avoid?
  2. When did your opinion of a character change?
  3. What did the setting add to the story? Could it happen anywhere else?
  4. Which scene would you cut, and which would you make longer?
  5. What do you think happens to the main character after the last page?
  6. Did the ending feel earned or rushed?
  7. What question would you ask the author?

Warm-up and closing questions

  • Warm-up: Where and when did you read most of it? Did you finish, and if not, where did you stop?
  • Rating round: Out of 5, and in one word, why?
  • Closing: What will you remember about this book in a year? Would you recommend it to the club's next new member?

Use the rating round last, not first, so early scores don't steer the conversation.

How do you use AI to write questions for a specific book?

An AI coach can draft questions for any book in a minute, which saves the question lead an evening. Give it the title, the author, your group and the tone you want, then ask for more questions than you need and pick the best six. Always check that the questions match what is actually in the book.

  1. Act as a book club host. Our group of [number] [describe members] read [title] by [author]. Write 12 discussion questions: 3 warm-up, 6 about the main ideas, 3 that connect the book to our own lives. Make them open-ended and avoid spoilers before question 7.

  1. Here are our notes from the last meeting: [notes]. Suggest 3 follow-up questions for the next session that build on what we disagreed about.

You can paste these into any AI chat. In Zehn, the Ask AI button on each book page answers questions about that specific book, which helps when you want to check what a chapter actually says.

How should the host run the discussion?

  • Ask a question, then wait five seconds before rescuing the silence.
  • Invite a quiet member by name with an easy question (“what did you think of chapter 2?”).
  • If two people debate for too long, ask a third person which side they're on.
  • Stop at the agreed time, even mid-conversation. Leftover energy carries into next month.

Questions people ask

How many questions does a book club need?

Six to eight good questions usually fill a one-hour meeting, because the best ones lead to follow-ups and stories. Prepare ten or twelve so the host can skip the ones that don't land. Start with one easy warm-up, spend most of the time on ideas and finish with a question about what members will actually do.

Who should prepare the discussion questions?

Rotate the job. A different member prepares the questions each month, usually the person who picked the book or the host. Rotation spreads the work and gives every meeting a slightly different flavour. The organiser can keep a shared document of past questions that worked well, so nobody starts from zero.

Can AI write good book club questions?

AI is good at drafting many open-ended questions quickly, especially for well-known books. It can also make mistakes about plot details or invent things the book doesn't say. Ask for more questions than you need, delete anything you can't confirm, and keep the ones that connect to your group's real lives.

What if nobody talks at the meeting?

Start with a round where everyone answers the same easy question, such as one sentence about where they read the book. Then ask for opinions, not facts. Personal questions like “where did the book not fit your life?” get quieter members talking. If the group is very quiet, try smaller breakout pairs for five minutes.
